hints: Look at what each test tells you separately, starting with 2,4-DNPH and Tollens' reagent to narrow down the carbonyl type.
An orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH but no change with Tollens' means you have a ketone, not an aldehyde.
A yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine means a methyl ketone group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so find the ketone that contains this group.
walkthrough:
**Use 2,4-DNPH to spot the carbonyl**

2,4-DNPH gives an orange precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone. Here we get orange ppt, so the unknown must contain a $\text{C}=\text{O}$ carbonyl group.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone + 2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange ppt}$$

**Use Tollens to rule out aldehydes**

Tollens' reagent oxidises aldehydes to give a silver mirror, but has no reaction with ketones. No change here means no aldehyde is present.

So combining Step 1 and Step 2, the compound must be a ketone.

**Use alkaline iodine to spot a methyl ketone**

Alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ is the iodoform test. A yellow ppt of $\text{CHI}_3$ forms only when the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ is present.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-\text{R} + \text{I}_2 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 \text{(yellow ppt)}$$

**Match to the structures**

We need a ketone containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. Option B is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COCH}_3$, pentane-2,4-dione, which is a ketone and has two methyl ketone groups. It fits all three results perfectly.

options.A: This is $\text{ICH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, an aldehyde. It would give orange ppt with 2,4-DNPH, but it would also give a positive Tollens' test (silver mirror). Since Tollens' shows no change, this cannot be correct.
options.B: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COCH}_3$, a diketone with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ groups. It gives orange ppt with 2,4-DNPH (ketone present), no change with Tollens' (not an aldehyde), and yellow ppt with alkaline $\text{I}_2$ (methyl ketone present). It matches all three tests.
options.C: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, pentanal, an aldehyde. Like option A, it would give a positive Tollens' test. It also lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so it would not give yellow ppt with alkaline iodine.
options.D: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I}$, a ketone but not a methyl ketone. It would correctly give orange ppt with 2,4-DNPH and no change with Tollens', but it has a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}-$ group, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so it fails the iodoform test.
